messages.subject: RE: plot with 2 y axes
messages.body_plain:
Hi Mario,

Plotting on left  and right y-axis can be done using base graphics package.
The broad approach is to overlay the second series on first series by using
par(new = TRUE)) and display the scale using axis(4). I am reproducing the
example code below which I got from other source.

y1 <- cumsum(rnorm(100))
y2 <- cumsum(rnorm(100, mean=0.2))

par(mai=c(.8, .8, .2, .8))
plot(1:100, y1, type="l", col="blue", xlab="X axis label", ylab="Left
legend")
par(new=TRUE)
plot(1:100, y2, type="l", ann=FALSE, yaxt="n")
axis(4)
legend(x="topleft", bty="n", lty=c(1,1), col=c("blue","black"),
       legend=c("String 1 (left scale)", "String 2 (right scale)"))

I tried to accomplish the same using ggplot2 and even posted a query here
some time back, for which no satisfactory reply so far. I still love to see
if some one could offer a solution using ggplot2 because of the amazing
charts it produces.

Regards,

S.N.V. Krishna

messages.subject: Re: ggplot2 and weights
messages.body_plain:
Hi:

I don't know if you can do weighted linear regression inside of ggplot2, but I wouldn't expect it to be so. Perhaps someone else can show how it's done, if at all. Looking at the help page of stat_smooth(), there is no input argument for weights, so it would seem to be safer to fit a weighted model outside of ggplot2. Below is some code for weighted simple linear regression outside of ggplot2,where I created a data frame of predictions and then generated the equivalent of geom_smooth() manually.

wtdlm <- lm(mpg ~ hp, data = mtcars, weights = cyl)
mp <- as.data.frame(cbind(hp = mtcars$hp,
                                           predict(wtdlm, interval = 'confidence')))
# Base plot
p1 <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = hp, y = mpg)) + geom_point(aes(size = cyl))
# Add the fitted model + confidence envelope
p1 + geom_line(data = mp, aes(x = hp, y = fit), size = 1, color = 'blue') +
        geom_line(data = mp, aes(x = hp, y = lwr), color = 'gray80') +
        geom_line(data = mp, aes(x = hp, y = upr), color = 'gray80') +
        geom_ribbon(data = mp, aes(x = hp, ymin = lwr, ymax = upr), alpha = 0.1)

It's not neatly packaged, but neither is it overly hard to produce. If you don't want the SE bars, eliminate the second argument in predict(); then, the single line of p1 + geom_line(...) without the plus sign at the end should be enough.

If you were not already aware, one of the nice things about ggplot2 is that you can add _compatible_ layers using data in different data frames. In this case, 'compatible' means the same x-variable and the same y-scale.

You can see that the fitted line above is not the same as the fitted LS line from geom_smooth() with

last_plot() + geom_smooth(data = mtcars, method = 'lm', size = 1, color = 'red', se = FALSE)

HTH,
Dennis

Such doubt and skepticism! ;)

You just need to use weight as an aesthetic:

qplot(hp, mpg, size=cyl, data=mtcars)+
  stat_smooth(method="lm", aes(weight=cyl))

But I totally agree that when you're doing a more complicated model
it's much better to do it outside of ggplot so that you can check that
it's doing what you think it's doing.

	geom_point() +

	geom_line(aes(group=ID)) +
	facet_grid(Sex ~ Drug)

I'm not sure your clarification made it to the whole group (didn't see
it just now), but Ista's (second) solution does do what you want.  Here
is a slightly different approach that gives the exact same plot that
Ista's solution does.

df <- data.frame(ID=factor(1:10),

         Sex=rep(c("male", "female"), 5),
         Drug=rep(c("Drug1", "Drug2"), 5),
         pre_D1=c(10:1),
         post_D1=c(1:10),
         pre_D2=c(25:16),
         post_D2=c(16:25))
dfm <- melt(df, id=c("ID", "Sex", "Drug"))

dfm <- cbind(dfm,
	colsplit(dfm$variable, "_", names=c("timing","D")))

ggplot(dfm, aes(variable, value)) +
         geom_point() +

         geom_line(aes(group=interaction(ID, D))) +
         facet_grid(Sex ~ Drug)

The only real difference between our solutions (aside from trivial
indenting/formatting) is how the D1/D2 information is extracted into its
own column (assignments with grep versus using colsplit) and how the
ultimate line grouping is specified (a separate variable combining ID
and D versus using interaction in the group specification avoiding
creating a new variable)

messages.subject_clean: Transporting mclust() plot elements into ggplot
messages.body_plain:
All,

I'm using mclust() to perform cluster analysis on some data. The plots
that are automatically generated by mclust contain cluster information
both as shape and color, which would be easy enough to pull into
ggplot. Several of the default plots also contain cluster centers that
are plotted as ellipses determined by the variance of the clusters.
I've done the rest of the plots for my thesis in ggplot and would like
to be able to transport these plots into ggplot as well to keep things
the same.

I am wondering if anyone is familiar with how mclust() plots are
created and what elements I need to pull out to create the cluster
center ellipses in ggplot. I've been trying to figure it out but I'm
not getting it.

Thanks in advance

messages.subject: use of stat_summary with a factor
messages.subject_clean: use of stat_summary with a factor
messages.body_plain:
I often use plots like the enclosed to describe the between- and
within-group variability in data.  (The line joins the average
responses for each group). That plot was created with lattice as

data(Dyestuff, package="lme4")
dotplot(reorder(Batch, Yield) ~ Yield, Dyestuff,
           ylab = "Batch", jitter.y = TRUE, pch = 21, aspect = 0.32,
           xlab = "Yield of dyestuff (grams of standard color)",
           type = c("p", "a"))

I tried to create a similar plot using ggplot2 and got as far as

qplot(reorder(Batch, Yield), Yield, data=Dyestuff,
      geom="point", pch=21, xlab=NULL,
      ylab="Yield of dyestuff (grams of standard color)") +
    stat_summary(fun.y = mean, geom="line") + coord_flip()

but the line I was hoping for didn't materialize.  Earlier I had used
position=position_jitter(w=0.1,h=0) in the call to qplot() but I
pulled it in case the jittered values were considered the x values
when grouping the y's.  However, even without the jittering I seem to
be unable to add the line, perhaps because one scale is a factor.

Suggestions welcome.

messages.body_plain:
Hello ggplot2 users,

First of all I would like to apologise because I’m very new to R and
therefore also to the package ggplot2; I’m writing to this forum
because I hope to find here some help for a definitive and neat way to
deal with my sort of personal “chart puzzle”.
I’ve been trying various solutions with so many different softwares
but none of them was plainly satisfactory to me.
In very short what I would like to do with R is the following type of
chart: https://sites.google.com/site/wantedchart/

a scatter plot with both x and y axes set in logarithmic scale, points
plotted with x and y error bars, leading lines to legend points to be
positioned at given specific positions in the chart frame (in order to
avoid label overlapping)

Can anyone please give me some “boostraping hints” from where and how
is better to start with?
Yes, I know I should have posted this message after a careful reading
of available documentation but I’m really somehow lost in the middle
of the forest of the R commands; I’m not looking for a pre-cooked
solution for my problem but rather an indication of the right path to
follow…

So far I’ve done a very much basic scatter plot without any useful
control on axis scales and most of all on the plotting of the error
bars and the point legends and the corresponding leading lines….again,
in short I’m hopeless!

Thank you very much for any help

maxbre

messages.body_plain:
Seems like we just had our wires crossed thanks to some gmail timewarping.

You should be really close now though. You can do the calculation in the geom_errorbar() and geom_errorbarh() calls. See their help pages for details. http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/

A bit more tweaking of the sizes and you're mostly there. The only thing that isn't nice is the justification. You should be able to supply a vector of justifications, one for each label in the order of the levels. hjust = 0 for labels on the right and hjust = 1 for labels on the left. At least I think you can do this.

I sure hope you're making more than one of these...

B

Not that I know of... perhaps the usual pros can chime in on this?

> It is just to generalise the script for other data sets I might be
> using...

I thought this is where you were going. You'll have to play around with the sizes of things and some different datasets to make sure things still look right.

Something like...
if (max(diox$x_avg> 1000)){
dot.size = 5
} else if (max(diox$x_avg> 500){
dot.size =3
} else {
dot.size = 1
}

then...

ggplot(diox, aes(x_avg, y_avg))+
geom_point(size=dot.size, colour = "blue")+

geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=y.lower, ymax=y.upper),width=0.1,size=0.1, colour = "red")+
geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin= x.lower, xmax= x.upper),height=0.1,size=0.1, colour = "red")+
geom_text(aes(label=labels, x = x_label, y = y_label), size=3, hjust=0)+
geom_segment(aes(xend = x_label, yend = y_label), linetype = "dashed")+
geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1)+
scale_y_log10()+
scale_x_log10()

 Is it possible to complete the type of the wiskers with a short
> perpendicular line, like in the example I posted here
> https://sites.google.com/site/wantedchart/

You can adjust the size of the wisker using the width = and height = attributes of geom_errorbar() and geom_errorbarh(), respectively.

> this blessed forum is really great
>
> max

messages.subject: facet_window or facet_page
messages.body_plain:
I was wondering if there was a way in ggpot2 to create a new faceting
option per page or window.
I often have data sets with 100 or more groups. If I use facet_wrap or
facet_grid I get the plot I am looking for but the facets are too
small to be of any use. I often have to resort to subsetting the data
to maybe 25 groups before plotting in ggplot2 and then plotting the
data 4 times to get all 100 groups down in graphs.

If there were a way in ggplot2 to be able to add an option in faceting
to wrap 25 groups per graph and then output 4 separate graphs, that
would save many steps. But I understand if this sort of thing is
beyond the capabilities of ggplot2. I was just thinking that maybe it
would be a nice feature to add to a future release of ggplot2 or if
somebody new of a method to do something similar by placing ggplot
with a plyr function.

Dan Gillie

messages.subject: Re: facet_window or facet_page
messages.body_plain:
You can create lists of individual plots and then plot them as you wish, like the following. But it doesn't make use of the faceting - so you'd have to manually (by way of a function) facet outside of ggplot2.

plt = list of ggplot objects
nrow, ncol = number of plots per page

function(plt, nrow, ncol)
{
loops <- ceiling(length(plt) / (nrow * ncol))
p <- 1
for (l in 1:loops) {
grid.newpage()
pushViewport(viewport(layout=grid.layout(nrow, ncol)))
for (r in 1:nrow) for (c in 1:ncol) {
if (p > length(plt)) break
print(plt[[p]], vp=viewport(layout.pos.row=r, layout.pos.col=c))
p <- p + 1
}
}}

Adam Loveland

messages.subject: Grouping and summing challenge
messages.body_plain:
I have longitudinal data for various entities that are themselves organized into groups, something like

day <- c(1,1,1,2,2,2,3,3,3)
group <- c("A","A","B","A","A","B","A","A","B")
entity <- rep(c("a","b","c"),3)
value <- c(5,12,7,4,8,9,13,4,5)
df <- data.frame(day,group,entity,value)

I'd like to use facet_wrap() to plot the A and B group data as line charts, with aes(x=day,y=value).

I failed to figure out how to do the grouping and summing inside ggplot, so I tried

dfcast <- data.frame(cast(df, day + group ~ ., fun.aggregate=sum))
colnames(dfcast) <- c("day","group","total")

(that I had to cast the result of cast as a data frame surprised me) and then

qplot(day, total, group=group,geom="line",data=dfcast)

That plots the data on one graph, but it does get the data right.  These next two examples seem closer to what I want, but they don't work:

## > qplot(day, total, geom="line",data=dfcast) +facet_wrap(~ group)
## Error in dim(out) <- c(1, nrow(.$facet_levels)) :
##   dims [product 2] do not match the length of object [0]

## > qplot(day, total, group=group,geom="line",data=dfcast) +facet_wrap(~ group)
## Error in dim(out) <- c(1, nrow(.$facet_levels)) :
##   dims [product 2] do not match the length of object [0]

Any tips on what to do differently?

Thanks,

Bill

messages.subject_clean: aes_string geom_text in a function "Object not found"
messages.body_plain:
This is a bug with the way that aes_string (and aes) work - they
currently don't capture the environment in which they are created, so
they don't have access to variables that aren't in the global
environment.  This is something I hope to fix in a future version -
it's something I've only recently figured out how to properly.

Hadley

messages.subject: Setting timezone for breaks and labels
messages.subject_clean: Setting timezone for breaks and labels
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have a some data that consists of pairs of timestamps and values.
The timestamps are recorded in the timezone GMT.
Recording starts at 00:00 GMT and last for 3 days.

My own timezone is CEST.

I would like to make scatter plot of this, but show the data as it would appear in the original timezone (GMT).
I tried this with adding a

   scale_x_datetime( tz="GMT")

However the data appeared as it had been shifted by about 2 hours.
The graphs shows days on the major break lines. The data starts about 2 hours from the first major break line.

A complete example is:

start <- ISOdate(2001, 10, 10, 0, tz = "GMT")
d <- data.frame(
        tms   = c( start, start + round(runif(20, max = 3 * 86400) ) ),
        val   = runif(21) )

p <- ggplot(d, aes(x=tms,y=val)) +
     geom_point() +
     scale_x_datetime( tz="GMT")

After some experimenting I found that the major breaks are displayed in my timezone,
while the data is displayed in the GMT timezone.

This can be seen with:
     scale_x_datetime( format = "%d/%b %H:%M", tz="GMT")
It shows that the first break is on:
    09 Oct 22:00 hours

Is there are way to also have the breaks and labels on the x-axis to be shown in the GMT time zone?

Have fun,
Frans.
